_meta.indication: Adjunctive treatment to glucocorticoid replacement to control androgens in adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH).

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial NBI-74788-CAH3003 (Trial CAH3003), in adults with classic CAH
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, stratified randomization 2:1; 24-week double-blind period followed by 24-week open-label period; 54 centers in 16 countries
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with classic CAH due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: percent change from baseline in glucocorticoid daily dose at Week 24 while Week 24 androstenedione levels are controlled (≤120% of baseline or ≤ULN for age and sex)
pivotal_trials.result: Glucocorticoid daily dose lowered by 27% (SE 2.4) vs 10% (SE 3.2) placebo at Week 24; treatment difference -17% (95% CI -24, -10). Key secondary: serum androstenedione at Week 4 decreased 299 (37.7) ng/dL vs +46 (51.0) ng/dL placebo; treatment difference -366 ng/dL (95% CI -457, -232). 63% of crinecerfont vs 18% placebo reduced to physiologic glucocorticoid dose at Week 24.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Trial NBI-74788-CAH2006 (Trial CAH2006), in pediatric subjects aged 4 to 17 years
pivotal_trials.design: Double-blind, placebo-controlled, stratified randomization 2:1; 28-week double-blind period followed by 24-week open-label period; 37 centers in 10 countries
pivotal_trials.population: Children ages 4 to 17 years with classic CAH due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: change from baseline in serum androstenedione at Week 4 while glucocorticoid dose stable
pivotal_trials.result: Serum androstenedione at Week 4 lowered -197 (39.4) ng/dL vs +71 (56.2) ng/dL placebo; treatment difference -268 (95% CI -403, -132). Key secondary: glucocorticoid daily dose at Week 28 lowered 18% (1.8) vs +6% (2.6) placebo; treatment difference -24% (95% CI -30, -17); and 17-hydroxyprogesterone at Week 4 lowered 5865 ng/dL vs +556 ng/dL placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in adults (≥4% and > placebo): fatigue (25% vs 15%), headache (16% vs 15%), dizziness (8% vs 3%), arthralgia (7% vs 0%), back pain (6% vs 3%), decreased appetite (4% vs 2%), myalgia (4% vs 3%). In pediatrics: headache (25% vs 6%), abdominal pain (13% vs 0%), fatigue (7% vs 0%), nasal congestion (7% vs 3%), epistaxis (4% vs 0%). Serious adverse events of acute adrenal insufficiency occurred in both trials in the setting of physiologic stress.
target_moa: Crinecerfont is a selective corticotropin-releasing factor (CRF) type 1 receptor antagonist; it blocks CRF binding to pituitary CRF type 1 receptors, inhibiting ACTH secretion and thereby reducing ACTH-mediated adrenal androgen production.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was convened because FDA determined the application did not raise issues requiring input from external experts.

basis.text: Breakthrough Therapy designation granted December 1, 2023; met criteria based on preliminary clinical data showing substantial improvement over available therapy via statistically significant reductions in daily glucocorticoid dose while maintaining androgen control.

requirement.text: 4738-1 Perform a lactation study (milk only or mother-infant pair study) in lactating women who have received Crenessity to measure concentrations of crinecerfont and its major metabolites in breast milk and to assess the effects on the breastfed infant.

citations.quote: 4738-1 Perform a lactation study (milk only or mother-infant pair study) in lactating women who have received Crenessity to measure concentrations of crinocerfont and its major metabolites in breast milk using a validated assay and to assess the effects on the breastfed infant, if a mother-infant pair study is conducted.

requirement.text: 4738-2 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Crenessity during pregnancy to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant, with infant outcomes assessed through at least the first year of life.
